references.text: Isaiah 61:1-2 is the direct prophetic source text that Jesus reads aloud in the synagogue at Nazareth. "To proclaim a year of favor from the Lord" (שְׁנַת־רָצוֹן לַיהוָה) is what Jesus quotes in Luke 4:19. The expression "the acceptable year of the Lord" (ἐνιαυτὸν κυρίου δεκτόν) is a direct rendering of this.

The Jubilee law in Leviticus 25 describes the Year of Jubilee, the 50th year, when liberty is proclaimed for all inhabitants of the land. The term "the Lord's year of favor" in Luke 4:19 has a deep connection to the liberation of the Jubilee—debt cancellation, release of slaves, and return of land—as an image of messianic salvation.

Isaiah 49:8 speaks of a "time of favor" and a "day of salvation" when the Lord hears his servant. This corresponds with the idea of "the acceptable year of the Lord" in Luke 4:19 as a time of divine grace and salvation.

Isaiah 58:6 deals with breaking the chains of injustice, setting the oppressed free, and breaking every yoke. This text is closely linked to the message of liberation in Luke 4:18-19 and is part of the Isaianic vision of the Lord's year of favor.

Paul quotes Isaiah 49:8 and says: "In a time of favor I heard you, and on a day of salvation I helped you. See, now is the time of favor; now is the day of salvation!" This connects to Luke 4:19 by pointing out that the messianic time of favor has now broken in.

Isaiah 42:7 refers to the Lord's servant who will open blind eyes and lead prisoners out of darkness. This is part of the same prophetic tradition underlying Jesus' proclamation of the Lord's year of favor in Luke 4:19.

Right after reading the passage from Isaiah, Jesus declares: "Today this scripture has been fulfilled while you were listening." This shows that "the acceptable year of the Lord" in verse 19 is now fulfilled through Jesus' coming and ministry.
Jesus' answer to John the Baptist's disciples summarizes his messianic works—the blind see, the lame walk, lepers are cleansed—as a concrete fulfillment of the year of favor proclaimed in Luke 4:19.
